title: Toner for dry skin: how to choose one, and which suits oily or sensitive skin
body:
A face toner is the light, watery step between cleansing and moisturising. Old-fashioned toners were often astringent and full of alcohol, which is why many people with dry skin still avoid them. Today most toners are gentle and hydrating instead. Here is how to choose a toner for dry skin, which toner suits oily or sensitive skin, and how to use one.

What does a toner do?

After cleansing, a toner takes off any last traces of cleanser or tap water and gives skin a first layer of moisture. Skin that is slightly damp takes serum and moisturiser more evenly, so a toner makes the rest of your routine easier to apply. It is an optional step: if your skin feels comfortable without one, you can skip it.

How to choose a toner for dry skin

  • Look for hydrating ingredients such as glycerine, rose water or aloe near the top of the list.
  • Avoid a high level of alcohol (listed as alcohol denat. or SD alcohol), which can leave dry skin feeling tight.
  • Keep it short if your skin is sensitive too: fewer ingredients make it easier to see what suits you.
  • Go easy on acids such as glycolic acid, which gently exfoliate. Dry skin may prefer them two or three times a week rather than daily.

Hydrating toners for dry and sensitive skin

Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99, 100ml) is the simplest toner we stock: just rose (Rosa centifolia) and distilled water, with no alcohol. It is a classic rose water toner that you can spritz on or sweep over with a cotton pad, and it also works as a midday refresher over bare skin. It is a good first toner for dry or sensitive skin.

Highborn London Diamond Toner (£25, 100ml) is a moisturising toner made to follow Highborn London Crystal Cleanser (£24) as the second step of the Highborn routine. Press it in with your hands or sweep it on with a cotton pad before serum and moisturiser.

A toner with a gentle acid

Vilvah Milk Face Toner (£19.99, 100ml) is water and earth marine water with glycerin, a xylitol-based moisturising blend and rice milk extract, plus glycolic acid, a gentle exfoliating acid. That makes it a good fit for normal and combination skin that wants a smoother feel. If your skin is dry or sensitive, start with two or three evenings a week, and wear sunscreen during the day while you use it.

Toner for oily skin

Oily skin still benefits from a light, hydrating toner: stripping skin with alcohol can leave it feeling tight while it still looks shiny. Deyga Tea Tree Facial Toner (£14.99, 100ml) is three ingredients: tea tree, mulethi (liquorice root) and distilled water, and Deyga makes it without alcohol. Its fresh, herbal feel suits oily and combination skin. Tea tree is an essential oil, so patch test it first if your skin is sensitive. More ideas for oily skin.

Which toner suits you?

  • Dry skin: Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner or Highborn London Diamond Toner, every day.
  • Sensitive skin: the two-ingredient rose water toner, and a patch test first.
  • Normal or combination skin: Vilvah Milk Face Toner, a few times a week to start.
  • Oily skin: Deyga Tea Tree Facial Toner.

How to use a toner

  1. Cleanse with a gentle face wash such as Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99), then pat your face almost dry. Our guide to face wash for your skin type helps you choose.
  2. Apply the toner with clean hands or a cotton pad, pressing it over the face and neck. Avoid the eyes.
  3. While skin is still damp, apply a serum such as Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99). Read our face serum guide.
  4. Finish with moisturiser. Dry skin likes something richer, such as Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99); see moisturiser for your skin type.
  5. In the morning, add sunscreen as the last step.

Good to know

  • Toner is not a cleanser: it will not take off make-up or sunscreen on its own.
  • Rose water also mixes face packs: see our face mask guide.
  • Patch test any new toner on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Stinging, redness or flaking that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

summary: What a face toner does, how to choose a hydrating toner for dry or sensitive skin, which toner suits oily skin, and how to use one.
